title: SH2B #50 (Second Anal Tunnel to Lake Bash)
description: Come out to bike the rail trails from Hyak to Rattlesnake Lake. Booze on trail and and BBQ after at the lake. Two miles through a train tunnel then smooth ride over bridges and trails all the way down. Looks like we have 3-4 trucks to take the group up to the top. We all go down! Down! Down! WHEN: Sunday 18th August 2024, 10:00 am, load bikes and start driving up by 11:00 am WHERE: Rattlesnake Lake parking area HARES: Shackless!!! ([redacted]) COST: $5 WHY: Bashing downhill is fun! EXPECT: 26 easy miles Eagle, 26 easy miles Turkey. So easy that a 5-year-old can do it and has. Great views and fun ride. Hare will provide a booze check and circle beers. BRING: New shoes, bikes, bike repair kit, a jacket for the tunnel, light to see in the tunnel, your own water, stuff to barbeque. ON-AFTER: Barbeque at the lake: BYOBooze, meat, foods etc.

title: SH2B #51 (All Wheels Matter)
locationStreet: Lower Woodland Park Lower Woodland Park
description: Seattle Hash House Bikers H3 # 51 (All Wheels Matter) When: 13:00, 15 September 2024 Where: Lower Woodland Tennis Courts (where we do the beer mile) 5773 West Green Lake Way N, Seattle, WA 98103 https://goo.gl/maps/RLd2YQje5gt7aTVs5 GPS: 47.[redacted], -122.[redacted] Who: Cougar Rican What: All wheels welcome! So long as it has wheels, and does not require a license to operate, bring it to the bash! Skateboard? Yes. Skates? Rad. Scooters? Let me know I'll get some Capri-Suns for you. Bikes? Duh. Segways? Don't forget your pocket protectors. Seriously, all wheels. Show up on a unicycle. Bring a hoverboard. Fucking Heelys, I don't care. Just don't be lame and show up on foot. Bring: $5, mode of transportation, helmet, money, ID, orange slices, cool X-Games clips.

title: SH2B #52 (2025 Reboot)
description: What: Seattle Hash House Bikers #52 (2025 Reboot) When: 12:00, 27 April 2025 Where: Lower Woodland Tennis Courts (yes, same place we just did beer mile) 5773 West Green Lake Way N, Seattle, WA 98103 https://maps.app.goo.gl/doUmbc2XiF11rQA66 Who: Cougar Rican What: It's the yearly awakening of the SH2B! And because the last 2 years it's poured on us, forcing us to turn the April trail into a bar-to-bar, we're just gonna say it's tradition and do so this year as well. It's certainly not because I almost forgot to do one this month. Expect: 3 stops, 10ish miles total, every hill I can find. Also, MRJ said that if I put it some shiggy, this will double as the Rain City trail for this month. Bring: $3, bikes, helmets, ID, money for bar stops, locks so you don't end up walking the back half of trail, new tires

title: SH2B #54 (Your dad needs some exercise)
description: This is an A to B trail with optional bike/train back to the start. Taking transit or biking to trail will save you possibly going the wrong way before you go home after circle. WHEN: Sunday June 15th, High Noon WHERE: Green Lake Park and Ride (near Roosevelt Light Rail station) https://maps.app.goo.gl/eydF5R2H1SGpHZuTA GETTING HERE: Take the train, take the bus, ride your bike, they’re all great options HARES: Butt and her trusty steed Raxy COST: $5, plus cold hard bar money for some of the beer checks WHY: I’m almost always the only one biking to the hash, so come try biking and get lost on some nice and bikeable roads and hills around Seattle. We’ll get drunk along the way because biking drunk is way more fun than driving drunk. So ride your bike to a train, take it to trail, and get dronk in the summer with your bestest of bashing friends EXPECT: 12 miles true trail to circle, plus 8 bike miles back to start if you don’t want to take the train or go home from the end. 4 beer/cider/wine drink stops to get your legs tired, and your mouth yapping. Mostly nice bike lanes+paths and checks at the bottom of Seattle’s lovely hills. Good views. BRING: A bike that mostly works, your father to fix it when it breaks, a vessel for liquids, a helmet, proof of age, orca card, knee pads or other cute bike accessories.

title: SH2B #56 (Save an Ironhorse, ride a cowboy)
location: Rattlesnake Lake by the Rattlesnake Lake Cedar Falls Trailhead
description: SH2B #56 - Save an Ironhorse, ride a cowboy Grab your trusty metal steed and giddy-up to join the bash on its annual pilgrimage between Hyak at Snoqualmie Pass and Rattlesnake Lake in North Bend. Join us at 11am at Rattlesnake Lake by the Rattlesnake Lake Cedar Falls Trailhead parking area. From there we will sort out who has the best bike racks for shuttling the pack up to Hyak where we'll start our ride the Iron Horse back down to the lake. Remember to bring not only your bicycle, but also a Discover Pass for parking. Hash Cash $5 to make you holler. Message Hoodie if you think you've got what it takes to help with the shuttle arrangements. Yee-Haw

title: SH2B #57 (Sail Away & Ride)
description: Sunday September 21st 2025 SH2B #57 – Sail away and Ride. Hare: Dim Sum Free Run Meet at 10:00am at Pier #50 Water Taxi departs at 10:30am for West Seattle, (15 minutes sail) and then we will be cycling on. Why the early start? Because , for anyone driving their car to the start, or else, we want to beat the Seahawks crowd and potentially get some of those free sunday parking spots. Indeed, on that day, the NFL football game Seahawks vs. New Orleans Saints will start at 1:05 PM at Lumen field. "The West Seattle Water Taxi can accommodate 26 bicycles per sailing on the M/V Sally Fox and M/V Doc Maynard vessels, while the Spirit of Kingston vessel has a lower capacity of 14 bikes." "Bikes are welcome at no additional charge. Please walk your bike between the pier entrance and the Water Taxi. Bicycles are limited to 73" long and 15" wide. Bags and trailers may need to be disconnected prior to being placed in the bike rack to allow more space". On On! https://kingcounty.gov/en/dept/metro/travel-options/water-taxi/west-seattle#toc-sailing-schedule

title: SH2B #58 (Tour De Franzia)
description: Grab your bike, your e-scooter, or whatever wheels you feel safe drinking wine on and join us for our annual wineries and wheels extravaganza, the Tour de Franzia Where: Gas Works Park When: Oct 19th noon, hare away at noon 30 Who: Hood Whorenament for your haring pleasure How Much: $2 for start/circle beverages, bring your ID and money for winery stops What: A fermented grape addled romp to as many of the wineries as the hare can get us to through the hills and dales of Fremont/Ballard/Greenwood and beyond. If folks who don't bike wanna get in on this, let the hare know and maybe I'll give you key information to do this via Lyft/Uber instead. Bring: Bikes, money for wine, ID, saddle bags and backpacks to buy more wine with so Hoodie doesn't have a dozen bottles in her saddlebags for everyone at the end of the ride (this time), a vessel for start and end wine
